description: VPI-RTDP keeps a lower bound `L` and an upper bound `U` on `V*`, the optimal expected cost of each state. Trials follow the action that is greedy on `L`. While some successor has a large gap `U − L`, a trial samples by probability times gap, as BRTDP does. Then it samples by the *value of perfect information* (VPI): how much the choice at the current state could improve if a successor's value were known. The run stops when `U − L ≤ ε` at the start, and the policy is greedy on `U`; use it when the bounds are informative and only some successors can change the decision.

papers.authors: Scott Sanner, Robby Goetschalckx, Kurt Driessens, Guy Shani
papers.title: Bayesian Real-Time Dynamic Programming
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
